attacks.claim: Production runs 48 workers at batch 50, which is far above the 300 msg/s SES limit, so throttling will occur. Any SendBulkEmail error marks the whole batch as failed, writes every recipient to send_failures, excludes them from the issue, and continues with no retry. Throttled subscribers will be permanently dropped and shown as 'Not delivered'.
attacks.evidence: SEND_WORKERS=48 ... SES production account limits (us-east-1): 300 messages/second ... if err != nil { for _, r := range batch.Recipients { failures.Record(...) } ... continue }

attacks.claim: The QA evidence that the pipeline works at scale is invalid. Staging was throttled, and the team turned throttling off in the mock to get a passing run. The 11-minute, 0-failure result therefore says nothing about production behaviour under SES throttling.
attacks.evidence: Staging SES account limit is 14 msg/s; 4 workers were throttled intermittently, so QA ran with SES throttling simulated off via the sandbox mock

attacks.claim: Smart Send defaults to on for every publication and holds issues up to 18 hours with no stated exemption for time-sensitive or scheduled issues. The 40% of publications that are news outlets will have breaking news and election results delayed. Delivered-late news cannot be recalled, and the rollback only affects future holds.
attacks.evidence: Smart Send ... Issues are held for at most 18 hours. Enabled by default for all publications ... SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=on ... 4,480 of them (40%) are news or local-news outlets whose issues are time-sensitive (breaking news, election results, weather alerts)

attacks.claim: The launch post says Smart Send is live for every publication today, but the rollout plan ramps it 5% → 25% → 100% over three weeks. The public statement contradicts the plan and tells publishers nothing needs setting up when most will not have it on yet.
attacks.evidence: Smart Send Time is live for every publication today ... Nothing to set up; it's already on. vs. ramp SMART_SEND_DEFAULT by publication cohort: 5% (week 1), 25% (week 2), 100% (week 3)

attacks.claim: The 'up to 5× faster' public claim is not supported. The goal is 14 min to under 3 min (about 4.7×), and the only measured result is 11 min with 4 workers under simulated throttling. No production throughput has been measured.
attacks.evidence: Goal: cut median time-to-inbox for a 50k-subscriber issue from 14 min to under 3 min ... 50k-recipient issue end to end | 4 workers, batch 50 | Pass, 0 failures, 11 min ... every Inkwell issue reaches inboxes up to 5× faster

attacks.claim: The Smart Send claim that issues arrive 'when each reader is most likely to open it' is contradicted by the 71% within-±1h accuracy. The stated lift gate (≥3% vs control) has no control measurement in the QA results, so the rollout gate cannot be evaluated.
attacks.evidence: Smart Send Time: predicted hour within ±1h of actual top open hour, 2,000 sampled subscribers | 71% ... we'll deliver each issue when each reader is most likely to open it ... gated on open-rate lift ≥ 3% vs control

attacks.claim: No alert fires on silent batch failure. send.batch_failed and send_failures growth are on a dashboard only, and the pager covers queue lag and complaint rate. Because failed batches are dropped without retry, queue lag can stay normal while a large share of the issue is never delivered.
attacks.evidence: On-call pager: queue lag > 10 min, complaint rate > 0.1%. ... Dashboards: send throughput, `send.batch_failed`

attacks.claim: Rolling back to Sidekiq does not undo send_failures rows written during a bad run. Affected subscribers stay excluded from the issue and appear as 'Not delivered', and no replay or cleanup path is described.
attacks.evidence: Rollback (pipeline): set SENDER=sidekiq in the dispatcher; in-flight batches drain in < 2 min ... failures.Record writes to send_failures; those recipients are excluded from the issue's remaining sends

attacks.claim: The pipeline is cut over to 100% of sends on Monday with no canary, even though the throttling path has never been exercised with real SES limits. The '< 2 min' drain claim for rollback is also unverified.
attacks.evidence: Send pipeline v2: deploy Monday 09:00 UTC to 100% of sends ... in-flight batches drain in < 2 min

attacks.claim: Smart Send builds a per-subscriber profile from 90 days of open behaviour and is enabled by default. The artifact describes no subscriber-facing notice, consent, or opt-out, only a publisher-level toggle.
attacks.evidence: predicts each subscriber's most likely open hour from their last 90 days of opens ... Enabled by default for all publications; publishers can turn it off in Settings → Delivery

attacks.claim: Smart Send applies to every issue without any stated exception for scheduled sends, which was the top customer request. Publishers who schedule a send for a specific time may find it silently moved by up to 18 hours.
attacks.evidence: Top customer request in Q3: scheduled sends with time zone support (shipped in 2026.08). ... delivers each issue at that hour. Issues are held for at most 18 hours

attacks.claim: The 'Not delivered' report may show failures for emails SES actually accepted, such as after a context timeout, and the label shows raw SES status strings. Publishers could misread delivery status.
attacks.evidence: failures.Record(ctx, batch.IssueID, r.SubscriberID, errCode(err)) ... shown to publishers in the issue report under "Not delivered"

attacks.claim: No SES spend or budget estimate is given for the 50k-recipient sends, retries (none exist), or 25M/day ceiling. Cost exposure from holds or re-sends cannot be bounded from the artifact.
attacks.evidence: SES production account limits (us-east-1): 300 messages/second, 25M/day.

attacks.claim: Nominal capacity is 48 workers × ~25 msg/s ≈ 1,200 msg/s against a 300 msg/s SES cap. Worker count was not sized to the account limit, which increases the chance of throttling, and no backpressure is described.
attacks.evidence: SEND_WORKERS=48 ... Per-worker throughput | 1 worker, batch 50 | ~25 msg/s sustained

attacks.claim: On error the loop continues without Ack and with no retry or redelivery policy stated. Redelivery behaviour and duplicate-send risk on partial SES acceptance are undefined.
attacks.evidence: if err != nil { ... metrics.Inc("send.batch_failed") continue } ... q.Ack(ctx, batch)

attacks.claim: Behavioural profiling of subscribers under default-on settings may trigger notice or lawful-basis obligations in some jurisdictions. The artifact does not address this.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any legal review, subscriber notice, or lawful-basis statement for the 90-day open-history prediction

attacks.claim: No material security attack found on the send path. Recorded failures and SES configuration set are scoped to production, though the artifact does not state the SES IAM scoping.
attacks.evidence: SES_CONFIGURATION_SET=inkwell-prod

attacks.claim: Sending depends entirely on a single provider (SES) with no alternate transport in the new pipeline. The Sidekiq fallback is temporary and idle for only 14 days.
attacks.evidence: keep the Sidekiq sender deployed but idle for 14 days

attacks.claim: No accessibility attack found. The launch copy and report labels are plain text.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no accessibility-relevant UI change described

attacks.claim: Publishers must discover the Settings → Delivery toggle to avoid an 18-hour hold, adding friction to the default path.
attacks.evidence: publishers can turn it off in Settings → Delivery

attacks.claim: The alarm thresholds (bounce 4%, complaint 0.08%) are not tied to the cohort ramp gates, so the Smart Send 'issue arrived late' ticket gate has no metric in the monitoring list.
attacks.evidence: 'issue arrived late' support tickets < 20/week
